plaintext.source: No contemporary decipherment visible in the available images; no independent edition located.

transcription.source: DECODE full-resolution images IMG_R7524_I33989_P1 and P3 (main checkout targets/potocka1714/, git-ignored)
transcription.notes: r7524-words.txt (5 Oct 2026) keeps the writer's word division: 53 cipher words, 232 figures, 77 distinct; clear Polish and Latin words in brackets. The older flat files r7524-cipher.txt and R7524-tokens.txt read 30 at figures 46 and 201 where r7524-words.txt reads 36 (P1 shows 36 at figure 46; checked 14 Oct 2026); counts are the same either way.

system.summary: A numerical cipher of 77 distinct figures (12-157), written with the writer's word division, among clear Polish and Latin words; its design is not established.
system.notes: Dots join the figures of a word, gaps separate words, '=' joins a word across a line end (r7524-words.txt). One-figure words 12, 38, 56, 133; repeated words (22.118.82.36.31.81 x4) suggest a letter cipher with homophones, untested. Not Potocka's alphabet.

conditions.human_role: Selected the ten DECODE records to Jakub Dunin, of which this is the one in a different cipher.
tools: solve_r7524_words.py, solve_r7524_dict.py (Pasek + Gutenberg Polish period model, scratchpad only)

solution.what: Acquired cached DECODE metadata and full-resolution images for R7524 together with the nine Potocka letters (R7525-R7536) addressed to the same recipient.

Visual inspection: R7524 catalogue language is Polish and its figures run to 157, unlike the short French passages of the Potocka letters; a single solver across all the letters to Dunin is not justified.
R7524 transcribed from the images: 232 cipher figures with clear Polish and Latin anchors (r7524-cipher.txt).

Mniszech R7524 tested with Polish quintgram homophonic annealing, a tentative hetmanow crib, a tentative null 33/ch=130 and a unigram-regularized search (solve_mniszech*.py). No coherent decipherment; these are hypotheses, not recovered values.
Searches for Mniszech/Dunin cipher, the shelfmark and cipher terms found biographical and archive catalogue context but no decipherment.
Inspected the three cipher-key records in the local DECODE Sanguszko catalogue: R7515 numeric alphabet (a=5/10/15, two series) and R7460/R7461 (graphic signs). None fits R7524.
A 232-token synthetic Polish homophonic control with 75 observed symbols recovered only 49 positions (21.1%). Mniszech search failures are inconclusive, not evidence of impossibility.

R7524 re-read at full resolution from IMG_R7524_I33989_P1/P3: all 232 figures confirmed; the writer's word division (dots within words, gaps between, '=' at line breaks) recorded for the first time in r7524-words.txt (53 cipher words, single-figure words 12, 38, 56, 133; doubled 19.19 and 28.28). The clear word filed as 'Starosty horodly' is 'spraktykowawszy'.

R7524 word-boundary homophonic annealing (solve_r7524_words.py) with pl-modern and with a period model built from Pasek's memoirs (Wikisource) + Gutenberg Polish; also with cribs hetmanow and 15.20=ie.
R7524 dictionary-word annealing (solve_r7524_dict.py; 49k-word Pasek+Gutenberg list, char-model fallback): 34-36 of 53 words land in the dictionary but restarts disagree completely; no stable key.
Tested whether R7524's numbering is Barbara Potocka's table (base 14-39, homophone = 2x base; targets/potocka1714/key-potocka.json) shifted (-40..40) or scaled (x1-x4): nothing fits.

Entry split from potocka1714 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026). Compared r7524-words.txt with the flat files: they differ at figures 46 and 201 (36 vs 30); the P1 image shows 36 at figure 46. No new attack.

outcome.method_basis: Homophonic annealing (flat, word-boundary, dictionary-word, with cribs) on modern and period Polish models gave no stable key, and a matched 232-token synthetic control was recovered only to 21.1%, so the failure is inconclusive.
outcome.fraction_read_source: targets/mniszech1714/r7524-words.txt: 232 cipher figures, none with a value.

gaps.detail: 77 signs, word-divided; no matching key or plaintext located; flat, word-boundary and dictionary-word annealing (Sept-Oct 2026) do not converge and the matched control fails at this length; not declared impossible.

outcome.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from potocka1714, which keeps Barbara Potocka's nine letters in her own alphabet. A stronger solver for short homophonic Polish, or more of Mniszech's cipher correspondence, is needed.
